leo_sales: Running into a roadblock with Orchid Health. Security wants a 2-week POC but insisted: all inference + telemetry must stay inside the EU (no exceptions). Can hosted support that strictly and what's the pricing impact?

ana_se: Yes — hosted can be constrained to EU-only with a strict routing policy and EU-only logging buckets. Two common approaches for POCs: (A) Hosted EU-only (soft-tenant on our EU infra) or (B) Short-term Dedicated EU pool (reserved GPUs) if they need stronger tenancy or model weight isolation.

leo_sales: They also asked whether any subprocessors are US-based by default (they refuse any US subprocessors). Need exact list for the DPA addendum.

tara_sec: Quick note: our default EU hosted uses providers in eu-north-1, europe-west2, and eu-west-1. Current EU subprocessors: AWS EMEA, GCP Europe, and LogKeep GmbH for log processing. We can produce an EU-only subprocessor appendix for the POC.

leo_sales: What happens if EU capacity is saturated mid-POC? Customer said no cross-border failover is allowed.

ana_se: We can enable strict_region_pinning which disables any failover. Behavior: requests exceeding local capacity are rejected with 429 (rate/queue) or 451 (restricted). Example snippet we give customers:

```yaml
routing:
  type: strict_region_pinning
  allowed_regions:
    - eu-north-1
    - europe-west2
  overflow_behavior: reject
```

ana_se: We also offer a queuing window option (max_queue=500ms) if they prefer short waits instead of immediate reject.

tara_sec: Encryption: TLS in transit everywhere; for at-rest we support customer-managed KMS in eu-west-1 or a customer BYOK KMS endpoint. Also, we can ensure audit logs stored only in EU S3/GCS buckets.

vince_legal: For contract: we'll attach DPA + SCCs. If they need an enumerated EU-only subprocessor list in the contract, legal can append that for the POC term. If they demand subprocessor-level indemnities or SLA, that's an enterprise-level ask (likely needs Dedicated and legal approval).

leo_sales: Pricing ballpark? They want to know uplift vs standard hosted for the 2-week POC (small load).

ana_se: For a short POC at low QPS: Hosted EU-only (no guaranteed capacity) = ~+12% per-token housekeeping premium (due to reserved capacity and EU infra costs). If they want guaranteed capacity (Dedicated short-term), expect a setup + reservation fee; rough for POC: ~4 A100-equivalent slots reserved -> quote afterwards.

leo_sales: Can you draft one sentence I can paste into the customer email summarizing guarantees and cost?

ana_se: "Hosted EU-only: all inference, KV caching, and telemetry will be processed and stored in EU subprocessors only; strict region pinning prevents any cross-border routing. Expect an approximate +12% per-token premium for short POCs; Dedicated EU pools available for guaranteed capacity (separate quote)."

tara_sec: Add: "Customer-managed KMS and EU-only audit log retention are available; we will provide an EU subprocessor appendix for contract."

ci_bot: [infra-bot] New doc: eu-subprocessors-2026-03-10 published -> https://redwood.example.com/compliance/subprocessors/eu-2026-03-10

leo_sales: Thanks. Action items: (1) Ana to prepare the routing YAML + short SOW paragraph; (2) Vince to prepare DPA + EU subprocessor appendix; (3) Tara to share KMS/BYOK instructions and log retention note.

ana_se: I'll drop the routing yaml + SOW by EOD and include recommended max_queue options.

vince_legal: Will prepare DPA + addendum; ETA tomorrow morning.

tara_sec: I'll provide BYOK steps and a one-pager on subprocessors by region.

leo_sales: I'll reply to Orchid with a proposed Wed kickoff and include those bullets. Also asking whether they need model artifact residency (onboarding weights) vs only inference/telemetry.

ana_se: FYI if they need artifact residency (weights never leaving EU) recommend Dedicated/Private. Hosted can mirror artifacts to EU storage during onboarding but some onboarding tools may pull from global sources unless mirrored.

leo_sales: Noted. Will confirm and update. :white_check_mark:
